A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RADD research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original RADD language-modeling perplexities, sampling times, generation-order experiments, and generated examples in Section 4 and Appendices G–H.

after.justification: v3 retains original RADD experiments and adds medium-model results, numerical-precision comparisons, entropy measurements, and batch-size experiments in Section 4 and Appendices J–K.

M1.justification: The time-independent RADD architecture, four objectives, and cached Euler/Tweedie sampling procedures are retained. The four corresponding algorithm bodies match across versions. Added AO-ARM pseudocode and dynamic-minibatching explanations document implementation rather than establish a changed underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on OpenWebText and evaluate LAMBADA, WikiText2, PTB, WikiText103, and One Billion Words. Unconditional generation and generation conditioned on prefix/suffix prompts remain covered. Added model sizes, precision settings, and batch sizes do not introduce different datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 compares RADD against both SEDD-Euler and SEDD-Tweedie; v3's corresponding runtime comparison retains SEDD-Tweedie but omits SEDD-Euler. Table 1's comparator membership is unchanged, with SEDD-U/S renamed SEDD-Unscale/Scale.

E3.justification: v3 adds medium-model evaluation and switches the principal generation comparison from small RADD-t-DCE to medium RADD-λ-DCE. Main timing measurements move from a 4090 with batch size 8 to an A800 with batch size 16. It introduces fp64/fp32 categorical-sampling comparisons, unigram entropy, and a separate batch-size experiment. Reported RADD-DSE weight decay changes from 0 to 0.03 and dropout from 0.1 to 0.02.

E4.justification: Appendix J.4 adds precision-sensitivity experiments measuring perplexity and entropy, plus a caching-efficiency ablation across batch sizes 1, 2, 4, and 8. Existing scaling/time-conditioning ablations extend to medium models, and the generation-order analysis is revised using medium-model results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Averaging over generated samples remains the reporting practice; the new experiment's sample count changes evaluation design rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces all five RADD-DSE scores, including LAMBADA 51.83 to 49.57, alongside changed regularization; other small-model rows remain unchanged. v3 adds medium-model scores, entropy and batch-timing results, and replaces generation/order results under revised conditions. For example, v3 reports RADD-medium perplexity 81 under fp64 versus 22 under fp32 at 4096 steps. v2 Table 2 is retained unchanged as v3 Table 7.

T1.justification: v3 corrects the missing minus sign in the AO-ARM objective, Eq. (2.11), making it consistent with negative log-likelihood minimization. The principal theorems, assumptions, and proofs in Appendices B–E remain substantively unchanged; the new AO-ARM exposition largely restates existing mathematics.

C1.justification: v3 removes the abstract's quantified 'up to 3.5 times faster' claim and emphasizes faster sampling convergence in the introduction. The core claims about score factorization, time-independent RADD, objective equivalence, and performance on five language-modeling benchmarks remain.

C2.justification: v3 explains that fp32 categorical-sampling errors can act as unintended annealing, making low perplexity misleading. The earlier conclusion that AO sampling performs worse is replaced by agreement with converged fp64 diffusion sampling under the revised evaluation. It also adds explanations involving finite-data gradient estimation and GPU utilization, and explicitly limits direct applicability to absorbing rather than multinomial diffusion.

D1.justification: v3 adds AO-ARM training/sampling pseudocode, dynamic-minibatching details, Gumbel-sampling precision, training-token totals, and timing-hardware information. A reproducibility statement points to setup instructions in the already-linked repository. Most existing implementation documentation remains, although the explicit seven-million-parameter reduction is no longer reported.

R1.justification: Section 3.3 and new Appendix H explicitly acknowledge Hoogeboom et al.'s prior ARM–diffusion ELBO equivalence and position RADD's analysis as an alternative proof connecting four losses. New Appendix F compares Chen et al.'s sampler, while Section 5 clarifies differences from Sahoo et al. v3 also incorporates Zheng et al.'s categorical-sampling critique, substantially refining the work's positioning.

P1.justification: The six-section main narrative and much of the prose are retained. v3 makes localized rewrites, moves introductory notation into Appendix A, expands appendix explanations, reorders algorithm presentations, and adds contents and reproducibility statements. Citation style, affiliations, and conference-header wording also change.

P2.justification: v3 adds an architecture schematic and reorganizes the main plots, replacing the small-model perplexity-versus-NFE display with a medium-model perplexity-versus-time plot. It adds medium-model, precision/entropy, and batch-size tables, relocates the unchanged long-training table, and replaces generated-text figures. Table grouping, metric highlighting, captions, and conference layout are also revised.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves an important evaluation blind spot: v2 assessed generation without precision or diversity controls, whereas v3 demonstrates the fp32 annealing artifact through fp64/fp32 and entropy comparisons and revises the AO-sampling interpretation. Medium-model experiments and clearer attribution of prior equivalence results further strengthen the paper. Changed RADD-DSE regularization weakens attribution of its better scores to architecture alone, but the improved generation controls provide a substantial net gain in scientific reliability.
